answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. The practical consequence is a steady economy where reputation is earned slowly, spent carefully, and never inflated by a sudden influx of cheap accounts. Consider a sonnet as the anchor of the cost.
